sections.markdown:
## C — Getting your Nevada license: who needs one, validity periods, new residents, identity and SSN documents, Real ID, the Driver Authorization Card, residency proof and the tests
Knowledge domain: the front end of a Nevada Basic Class C application — who must hold a Nevada license, how long each card lasts, how new residents transfer, which documents prove identity, Social Security Number and residency, how Real ID and the Driver Authorization Card differ, and what the vision, knowledge and road tests involve.

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
Anyone who lives or works in Nevada and wants to drive on its streets and highways needs a Nevada license; employees from border states and military members stationed in Nevada are the stated exceptions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
Someone who moves to Nevada from another state has 30 days after becoming a resident to apply for a Nevada driver license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
An applicant fills out an application, visits a full-service DMV office, must be at least 16 years old, and proves full legal name, age, Nevada residency and a Social Security Number if one was ever issued. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
A Social Security Number is not needed to get a Driver Authorization Card (DAC). [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
A Nevada license or ID expires on the holder's birthday in the fourth or eighth year depending on age, unless limited-term immigration documents set expiration to the DHS-verified departure date or one year if unspecified [A01].
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
If limited-term immigration documents were used as proof of name and birth date, the license expires on the departure date verified electronically by DHS, or after one year when DHS supplies no date. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
Under NRS 483.290 a Nevada driver license or identification card can never be valid for longer than eight years. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
Licenses for drivers aged 65 and older are valid for four years, while identification cards are valid for eight years. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
An applicant under 18 needs a co-signer (a custodial parent, a legal guardian or another person allowed by NRS 483.300), and that co-signer shares liability for damage the minor causes by negligent or willful driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A02
A Nevada resident may hold only one driver license or ID card, so a card from another state, US territory or foreign country must be surrendered; it is voided and handed back. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A02
A new resident always takes the vision test, and the other tests can be waived only when every one of the listed transfer conditions is met. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A02
Waiver condition: fewer than 3 moving violations in the past 4 years, and no suspension, revocation or cancellation of the license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A02
Waiver condition: no DUI conviction within the past 7 years. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
Waiver conditions: no restriction on the driving privilege that calls for an evaluation, a valid out-of-state license of the same class being applied for, and an age of 21 or older. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
An active-duty member of the US Armed Forces who holds a valid home-state license does not need a Nevada license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A02
Non-residents such as out-of-state students, tourists and seasonal residents may drive in Nevada without a Nevada license if they are at least 16, hold a valid home-state license and obey Nevada traffic and financial responsibility laws. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A02
Every driver record is run through two national databases, the Problem Driver Pointer System and the CDL Information System, and a privilege suspended, revoked, canceled or denied elsewhere blocks a Nevada license until that issue is cleared, though an ID card may still be possible meanwhile. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A03
Proof of full legal name and date of birth is one unexpired original or certified document, for example a state-issued birth certificate, a valid US passport or passport card, a Consular Report of Birth Abroad (FS-240), or another state's license, permit or ID bearing a DHS-approved Real ID mark. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A03
A Nevada Department of Corrections ID card can prove name and birth date, but not for a Real ID. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A03
An out-of-state Real ID marked limited term does not prove name and birth date; acceptable immigration documents have to be shown instead. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A03
These do not prove name and age: a hospital-issued birth certificate, a license or ID from another US state, territory or foreign country, a foreign birth certificate, a Border Crossing Card or a Consular Identification Card. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A03
When your current name differs from your identity document, bring legal proof of the change such as a marriage certificate, a divorce decree that mentions the name change, a spouse's death certificate, an adoption record or a court order, as an original or certified copy. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A04
Proof of Social Security Number is a Social Security card, a W-2 or IRS Form 1099 showing the full number, or a paystub with full legal name; handwritten paystubs are refused and every document must be an original showing the complete number. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A04
Alternative documents for name, age and Social Security Number need supervisory approval and can never be used to issue a Real ID card. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A04
A Real ID license or ID shows a gold Nevada outline with a star cutout, while a standard card carries the words NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A04
Nevada applicants may choose either a Real ID compliant card or a standard card, and the DMV must verify identity, birth date, Social Security Number, lawful status and primary residential address. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A04
A Real ID applicant presents two documents proving Nevada residency that show the correct residential address, such as utility bills, mortgage statements, rental agreements or bank statements. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A05
A Driver Authorization Card is valid for four years, expires on the holder's birthday and must be carried whenever the holder drives; renewals and address changes are done in person only. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A05
For a DAC you may show one document from the main identity list, or one of a US military ID, a US military dependent ID, a US Armed Forces discharge document or a US Certificate of Degree of Indian Blood. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A05
A DAC applicant may instead show two documents from a second list: a license, ID or DAC from another state, DC or a US territory, a foreign passport, a foreign birth certificate, a Mexican Federal Electoral Card, a Consular Identification Card or a similar foreign-government document. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A05
A DAC is not valid for federal or state identification and cannot establish eligibility for Nevada benefits, licenses or services, and DAC application information is not used to decide legal presence or immigration status. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A06
Applicants for an original Real ID or standard ID card, instruction permit or driver license must prove a Nevada residential address, and DAC applicants must do so at original issuance. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A06
Residency is proven with originals or certified copies of any two listed documents showing a Nevada residential address; one group of documents must be dated within 60 days, the other group may be the last one issued. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A06
A hotel, motel, RV park or campground record counts as residency proof only if it shows at least 30 consecutive days of living in Nevada. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A06
For an applicant under 18, a parent or guardian can prove the applicant's residence with two listed documents or by signing a DMV-approved form confirming they share the same address. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A07
If you need glasses or contact lenses to meet the vision standard, a restriction is placed on your license. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A07
The knowledge test checks highway signs and markings, traffic laws and safe driving practices on automated equipment or paper; an oral exam can be requested and Basic Class C testing is also offered in Spanish. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A07
Initial knowledge and skills tests carry a $25 fee, and each retest needed before the license is issued costs $10. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A07
Before the road test the examiner checks the registration and plates, proof of insurance, headlights, taillights, brake lights, turn signals, horn, seat belts, tires and windshield wipers. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F40 | anchor: A07
The test vehicle must be safe with working brakes, speedometer and muffler and a clean, safe seat for the examiner, and no passengers or animals may ride along. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F41 | anchor: A07
The road test scores how you prepare, control the car, enter traffic, use lanes, control speed, turn, park, back up, stop, pass and watch traffic, and you may be asked to stop on a grade; breaking a traffic law during the test is penalized. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F42 | anchor: A07
Using a cell phone during the drive test is an automatic failure, and aids such as parking assist and cruise control may not be used. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0012]

Misconceptions: turning sixty-five shortens a new license to four years, it does not end it; a waiver for new residents never covers the vision test; a Driver Authorization Card lets you drive but is not identification; a limited-term Real ID from another state does not prove name and birth date; a phone used during the drive test fails it outright.
Mnemonics: thirty days to switch after moving in; eight, four, eight (under sixty-five, sixty-five plus, ID card); waiver needs few tickets, no DUI, no flags, same class, twenty-one.
Glossary: DAC means Driver Authorization Card, a driving-only credential that needs no Social Security Number; Real ID means the federal-standard card with the gold outline and star; Limited Term means a card tied to an immigration departure date; co-signer means the adult who signs a minor's application and shares liability.
Dynamic facts: test fees, accepted document lists, immigration-document rules and the DMV phone numbers and website can change; confirm them on the Nevada DMV website.
